note: kmers_in_target (SPEC section 3, since MetaGraph master #634): a coordinate query (query_coords) on a multi-graph server of two pairs. The rows of a pair with a .seqs record mapping (with_seqs: each label a record) carry kmer_coords (positions in the record), kmer_count and kmers_in_target, the record's k-mer count (its length - k + 1: 360 - 31 + 1 = 330), so kmer_count / kmers_in_target (70 / 330) is the fraction of the target the query's k-mers cover. The rows of a pair without a .seqs (without_seqs: each label a whole column, here a FASTA file) carry kmer_coords (positions in the column: set_1.fa holds the element in its two records, at 130 and at 330 + 130) and kmer_count, and no kmers_in_target; nor do signature or counts rows. kmer_coords lists runs "query k-mer position-first target k-mer[-last]" joined by ":". Each row is tagged with its pair, the rows in pair order, one cut per pair: with_seqs returns 2 of its 3 tied records (complete false, nth_score 70, tied 3), without_seqs both its columns (complete). A single-graph server states kmers_in_target alike, on untagged rows. A real run: the body is the server's answer unchanged (its pair_ids those of the paths as the graph list spells them, relative), each index_fp its pair's manifest's. T8-M6 (train 8, pair identity; SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 1.2): each pair is named by graph and pair_id, master's n1 id of the name and the two paths as the graph list spells them (the paths this sample stated before), and no configured path is stated; each cut states matched, the labels above the request's thresholds before the cut (master's member; returned where the cut is complete, all three tied records where with_seqs is cut).
